fact_en:
How much of a sailfin lizard is just tail?

More than half! A sailfin lizard can grow almost a meter long, and most of that length is its long tail.
fact_bis:
Pila ka bahin sa lawas sa sailfin lizard ang ikog ra?

Kapin sa katunga! Moabot ang sailfin lizard og hapit usa ka metro ang gitas-on, ug kadaghanan niini mao ang taas nga ikog niini.

findings.note: title_bis 'Tiki nga Layag' for title_en 'Sailfin Lizard'. 'Tiki' is the house gecko, a different animal from the sailfin lizard (ibid/layagan); the card's fact is that it reaches almost a metre with over half of that tail, which is false for a gecko. Body keeps the English name, so only the title misnames it.

fact_en: Every living thing has a life cycle: born or sprouts, grows, reproduces, then dies. Some animals go through metamorphosis too — like a butterfly (egg to caterpillar to pupa to butterfly) or a frog (egg to tadpole to frog)!
fact_bis: Ang matag buhi nga butang moagi sa life cycle: matawo o moturok, motubo, mosanay, ug mamatay. Adunay mga hayop nga moagi usab sa metamorphosis — sama sa alibangbang (itlog, tangkong, pupa, alibangbang) ug baki (itlog, ulo-ulo, baki)!

findings.note: Butterfly life cycle listed as 'itlog, tangkong, pupa, alibangbang'. 'Tangkong' is water spinach (kangkong), not a caterpillar ('ulod'). The correct word appears nowhere on the card, so the larval stage is unrecoverable - a child reads a vegetable as a life-cycle stage. The frog list ('itlog, ulo-ulo, baki') is fine.

fact_en:
Why does a cat lick itself?

A cat licks its own fur to clean itself — this removes dirt and tiny pests that could carry disease, keeping it healthy!
fact_bis:
Nganong gitilapan sa iring ang kaugalingon?

Gitilapan sa iring ang kaugalingong balhibo aron manghinlo — makuha niini ang hugaw ug gagmayng kuto nga makadala og sakit, aron magpabiling himsog!

findings.note: Cat card titled with the word for dog: title_bis 'Iro Dila Balahibo' (dog/tongue/fur) for title_en 'Cats Groom Themselves'. The body correctly uses 'iring', but the title itself names the wrong animal - the same defect class already confirmed in this corpus.

fact_en:
Why do ants walk in a line?

When a worker ant finds food, it leaves a special scent along the path. Other ants follow that scent, which is why we see them marching one after another in a line.
fact_bis:
Ngano nagsunod-sunod paglakaw ang mga langgam?

Kon makakita og pagkaon ang usa ka worker ant, magbilin kini og espesyal nga baho sa agianan. Ang ubang langgam mosunod niini nga baho, mao nga makita nato sila nga naglakaw nga sunod-sunod.

findings.note: Whole card swaps ants for birds. EN 'Why do ants walk in a line?' -> BIS 'Ngano nagsunod-sunod paglakaw ang mga langgam?' and 'Ang ubang langgam mosunod niini nga baho'; title_bis 'Baho nga Dalan sa Langgam'. In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (Tagalog false friend: langgam = ant). Only the stray English 'worker ant' hints otherwise, so a Cebuano-only reader learns birds follow scent trails in single file. Corpus elsewhere uses the correct 'hulmigas' (ffct-11049).

fact_en: Termite soldiers have large heads and strong jaws to defend the colony from predators like ants.
fact_bis: Ang mga sundalo nga anay adunay dako nga ulo ug lig-on nga apapangig aron panalipdan ang kolonya gikan sa mga manunukob sama sa langgam.

findings.note: EN: termite soldiers defend the colony 'from predators like ants'. BIS: 'gikan sa mga manunukob sama sa langgam' = predators like BIRDS. The named predator is a different animal and nothing in the card corrects it.

fact_en: A millipede won't hurt you at all, unlike a centipede, it doesn't bite people.
fact_bis: Dili makadaot ang millipede, dili kini mopaak sa tawo, dili sama sa alupihan.

findings.note: title_bis "Millipede nga Dili Mokaon" (= does not EAT) for "Harmless Millipedes"; the body says dili kini mopaak (does not bite). The title asserts a separate false claim (millipedes don't eat) that nothing on the card corrects.

fact_en:
How many hearts does an earthworm have?

An earthworm doesn't have a true heart — instead it has five pairs of heart-like arches that pump its blood!
fact_bis:
Pila ka kasingkasing ang naa sa wati?

Ang wati walay tinuod nga kasingkasing — hinuon adunay lima ka pares nga arko nga morag kasingkasing nga nagbomba sa iyang dugo!

findings.note: title_bis "Lima ka Kasingkasing sa Buli" for "An Earthworm's Five Hearts": buli is not earthworm in Cebuano (buri palm / backside). The body uses the correct word wati, so the title names a different thing entirely.

fact_en:
Why does a bee die after it stings?

A worker bee's stinger has tiny barbs that get stuck in your skin—when it pulls away, part of its body tears off, and it dies.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga mamatay ang buyog human motusok?

Adunay gagmayng kawit ang tuslok sa buyog nga mahigot sa panit—kon mobira kini palayo, magisi ang bahin sa lawas niini ug mamatay.

findings.note: title_bis "Buyog sa Singhot" for "Why Bees Die After Stinging": singhot = to sniff/smell, not to sting. The body uses motusok/tuslok correctly, so the fact survives, but the title states the wrong action.

fact_en:
Are dogs the only pets with swivel ears?

Nope — cats can swivel their ears toward sounds too, so both pets are great at finding where a noise came from.
fact_bis:
Iro ra ba ang adunay malihok nga dalunggan?

Dili diay — makahimo usab ang iring sa pagtuyok sa dalunggan padulong sa tingog, mao nga maayo silang duha mangita kung asa gikan ang saba.

findings.note: title_bis 'Iro Iro Dalunggan' for 'Dog Cat Swivel Ears' — says dog twice; the cat (iring) is gone, erasing the dog-vs-cat contrast the card exists to make. Body is correct ('iro ug iring').

fact_en:
Can touching a frog give you warts?

No! Handling a Philippine wrinkled frog won't give you warts — those are actually caused by the human papillomavirus.
fact_bis:
Makatakod ba og warts ang pagdapo sa baki?

Dili! Ang pagdapo sa Philippine wrinkled frog dili maghatag og warts — ang warts hinungdan sa human papillomavirus.

findings.note: title_bis 'Baki Dili Tinga' — 'tinga' is food stuck between the teeth, not warts (kulugo). The title states a different, unrelated claim about frogs; body keeps English 'warts'.

fact_en:
Do animals have a larynx too?

Yes! Dogs and cats have a larynx too — it's what lets them bark, meow, and make other sounds.
fact_bis:
Aduna ba say larynx ang mga hayop?

Oo! Aduna say larynx ang iro ug iring — mao kini ang makapatahol, makapangiyaw, ug makahimo sila og tunog.

findings.note: title_bis 'Larynx sa Iro ug Iro' — 'dogs and dogs' where the card is about dogs AND cats; body correctly says 'iro ug iring'. Same title defect as ffct-11324.

fact_en:
Why does a hedgehog curl up?

When scared, a hedgehog rolls into a tight ball — hiding its soft belly and pointing its sharp spines straight at any enemy!
fact_bis:
Nganong maglingin ang hedgehog?

Kon mahadlok, magalingin ang hedgehog sama sa bola — gitagoan ang humok nga tiyan ug giatubang ang mga tunok sa kaaway!

findings.note: title_bis 'Dagger sa Pagliko' for 'Hedgehogs Curl Into Balls' — the animal is missing entirely and an unrelated noun ('dagger') stands in its place; nothing in the title points to a hedgehog curling up.
